subject: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@acmeanalytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps

Hi all,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday, Sarah — the Acme team’s questions about per-route cost attribution and how tokens traverse our stack were very helpful. To make the Console actionable for customers like Acme I want to propose a concrete instrumentation ask we can scope quickly: a per-route "token-pathway" visualization that shows token counts, per-stage latency, sampling rate, and a cost attribution column (estimated $/1000 tokens) for the last 24h / 7d.

Attached is a rough mock (token_pathway_mock_v1.png) and the Acme doc with their specific requirements (acme_token_requirements.docx). High-level asks from Acme:
- Show token counts broken down by request path + model variant
- Surface heavy tail requests (p95/p99 token length) and associated cost
- Make sampling configuration visible and editable (sample rate + retention window)

Can the infra/telemetry team confirm which of these metrics are currently emitted by runtime (KV cache hits, batching size, per-request token_count, model_variant) and what additional traces/events we need to collect? I'd like to align on a minimal data schema we can ship as a beta in 3 sprints, and a follow-up plan for richer visualizations.

Next step proposal: quick sync today or tomorrow to align on telemetry gaps and a minimal demo for Acme by end of next week.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps

Priya — this is great, thanks for pulling it together. Quick notes from telemetry/runtime perspective:

- We already emit per-request token_count and model_variant in the request envelope for hosted API.
- KV cache hit/miss is currently logged but as an event per-inference node (not yet correlated to a per-request persistent id). We can add a correlation id to KV events with a modest change (1 sprint).
- Batching metadata (batch size, batch latency) exists at the worker level; we don’t currently roll that up per-request when requests are de-batched.

To deliver the "minimal data schema" for the beta we need: (A) a stable request_id that flows through batching and caching; (B) per-request aggregation of batch-level metrics (amortized batch cost, per-request latency contribution); (C) a small sampling flag so we can keep retention low for high-volume routes.

I can carve out engineering time to add request_id propagation + sampling flag — estimate: 2 sprints of focused infra work + a small console change to render the new fields.

Happy to join a sync today at 11am PT.

—Dylan
From: Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps

Thanks Priya & Dylan — A few product notes:

- UX: the mock is helpful. For the beta let's keep the UI a single table with expandable rows to show per-stage latency (ingest, batching, model, post-process). Avoid a full graph in day-one.
- Controls: expose sample rate (0.1% / 1% / 10% presets) and retention (7 / 30 / 90 days). Make the default conservative to protect telemetry costs.
- Alerts: we should add one alert template: route_token_cost_spike (threshold configurable) that ties into existing alerting workflows.

Also, quick ask: can the telemetry include a small "confidence" field for the cost estimate (low/medium/high) so customers understand when we're extrapolating from sampled data?

If we can get the telemetry changes Dylan proposed, I think the PM/UX scope is 1.5 sprints to ship the table + controls as a beta.

—Grace
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps

Looping in roadmap context: I agree this is high priority for customer expansion and for the Console value prop. A couple of commercial notes:

- Acme's procurement team flagged that clear cost-attribution views materially affect renewal conversations — they asked us to include an exportable CSV for chargeback.
- For SLAs we should highlight whether routes are using Dedicated vs Hosted; customers will expect different cost profiles.

I'll put a tentative commit for a proof-of-beta in sprint 56 (starts in two weeks) provided Dylan can scope the infra changes. Marcus, can you confirm whether we need any SRE-runbook changes (SLO exceptions, fallback behaviors) for sampled telemetry?

—Ben
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Connor <sarah.connor@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-pathway cost & latency map — instrumentation ask and next steps

Thanks — quick SRE notes:

- Sampling has operational implications: if we sample aggressively we may miss rare high-latency events. We should keep a small deterministic low-rate trace for tail-finding (e.g., 0.01% deterministic tail sample) in addition to randomized sampling for cost reasons.
- For fallback behavior: if token-pathway telemetry fails, Console should fall back to aggregate per-route metrics without token-level attribution and show a banner: "Token-pathway data currently unavailable — showing aggregated metrics."
- I will add a short runbook entry for how to triage token-pathway ingestion issues and how to toggle sampling rates.

Action items from me: add runbook stub + confirm SLO impact by EOD Friday.

Marcus
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference
